title: A world with no miracles
text:
Science believes in the assumption that the universe has always followed natural laws and continues to follow these laws. But this is only an assumption.
There is no proof that the natural laws were the same a few million years ago or they will remain the same tomorrow. All things in the universe might have recently come into the current configuration giving a false impression as if things have always worked the same way.
No scientist can guarantee with 100% surety that the universe will continue to follow the same laws tomorrow. The certainty comes only from the Creator Himself!
Once God issues a decree, it does not change. Neither does anyone else has the power to change His Will. God is not a human we could watch Him do things. God’s Sunnah (behavior / way of doing things) is expressed through His creation.
But, but, but …
If the universe was created by someone other than God, you could have asked God to demonstrate His Power by turning the sun colder, by splitting the moon into two, or by making the needle float on water. But these are petty human desires to show off. If you are not impressed by the gigantic galaxies, mysterious blackholes, and fiery stars, or by the tiniest subatomic particles and quarks, no miracle will be able to convince you of God’s Power!
God’s creation plan is based on His Wisdom and He knew what properties to assign to entities. God created the fire to burn. He does not need to change His original plan and stop fire from burning. Only Humans make changes because their knowledge is not perfect.
God used His Free Will to implement His decisions in measurable proportions, called natural laws, so that humans could discover and take advantage of these laws for the benefit of humanity. God has the Power to give any Command, but He “Willed” that His Command be actualized in “fixed laws”.

title: A world with no miracles
text:
No Miracles for the Messenger

They say, “If only a miracle could come down to him from his Lord! @{qxp| (then we would have believed in Him.) }@” Say, “God has the Power to send down a miracle, but most of them do not use their knowledge.” [Quran 6:37]

He does not wish to stun the human intellect with supernatural phenomena. He wants believers to reflect and use reason. See [Quran 12:108]

Those who deny the truth keep saying, “Why has no miracle ever been bestowed upon him from his Lord?” But you (O Prophet) are only a warner and to every community is a guide. [Quran 13:7]


And yet they say, “Why are not miracles bestowed upon him from his Lord?” Say, “These verses are in themselves miraculous signs concerning God and with Him are the miracles (that you can see in the Universe). As for me, I am but a plain warner @{qxp| (drawing your attention to His signs and to the consequences of your actions.) }@” [Quran 29:50]


Why! Is it not enough (of a miracle) for them that We have bestowed upon you this Book that is conveyed to them? For, herein is Grace, a Reminder, and it is a giver of eminence to people who accept it. [Quran 29:51]


(Though we did not, but) Even if We had sent down to you (O Prophet) a pre-printed book written on parchment (as a miracle), so that they could feel it with their hands, the rejecters would have said, ‘This is nothing but obvious trickery!’ [Quran 6:7]

title: The Quranic God
text: When God talks about Himself as a Being, He describes Himself as One, Unique, and Uncaused Cause, to Whom you find no comparison in the universe or in your imagination.

title: The Quranic God
text:
One God?
God is ONE. But what is the meaning of it? God is not something that we can see with our eyes and count. We know God through His creation. If there were multiple gods, each would have different opinion about running the affairs of the universe. This would have led to chaos and disorder in the universe. You do not need any degree or diploma to understand this simple concept.

Had there been gods besides Allah within the heavens and earth, both would have been ruined … [Quran 21:22]

Since there is no second God to override or modify the rules, the laws created by One God never change. But, the concept of ‘no change’ implies restrictions on wandering capricious Will. Has God imposed restrictions on Himself to not change? Let’s see what the Quran says about it.

, “To whom belongs all that is in the heavens and earth?” Say, “To God, [Who] has prescribed for Himself grace (”mercy”) [Rahmah] …” [Quran 6:12]

He has made it “mandatory” on Himself to provide [Rahmah]. He has similarly placed other restrictions on Himself.

Those who accept the Message and live upright. There is good news for them in this world and in the Hereafter. God’s Words never change … [Quran 10:63-64]

Nor does anyone else has the power to change His rules. Nor can one escape from His rules.

Completed is the Word of your Lord in truth and justice. None can change His Words. He is the Profound Hearer, the Knower. [Quran 6:115]


… None can alter His Words. And you will find no refuge other than Him. [Quran 18:27]

God is so uncompromising in His decisions, He does not deviate a bit, let alone make a complete replacement or His laws.

Nay, no change you will ever find in the Sunnah  (behavior, laws)  of God, and no deviation you will ever find in the Sunnah  (behavior, laws)  of Allah. [Quran 35:43]

God has created unwavering rules not only for the physical, but for the human life (Nafs / “soul”) and social life as well.

That was the Sunnah  (behavior, laws)  of God among those who lived before. And never will you find any change in God’s Sunnah  (behavior, laws) . [Quran 33:62]

Even a God’s messenger has no power to change any of these rules.

Messengers before you were denied and opposed … There is none to alter the Words  (Decisions, Decree)  of God … (remember they would still not believe) even if you were able to seek a tunnel in the ground or a ladder to the sky and bring them a miracle (on your own) … So, do not be among those who are swayed by ignorance  (about the free will.)  [Quran 6:34-35]

God wants His servants to reflect and make free choices. See [Quran 2:256] and [Quran 10:99]

title: The Quranic God
text:
God’s Expression [Sunnah]
We do not anticipate God’s actions [Sunnah] in the same way we do for humans, such as walking, talking, and eating, etc. So, what is the meaning of “God’s Words and His [Sunnah]?”

God either talks through His messengers via His Books, or through His Creation - the universe and its laws.

His Laws in Theory (Words of God = Kalimaatillah) and His Laws in Practice as implemented in the Universe (Actions of God = Sunnatillah) complement each other and do not contradict. Once He decides on something, He does not change His Mind. Humans change their mind. God is not a human.
See, how He invites us to see Him through His observable universe:

God is the One Who causes the grains and the seeds to split and germinate (according to His Sunnah.) He produces the living from the dead, and the dead from the living. Such is God. (This is how never changing Sunnah of God works.) Where are you headed in bewilderment (looking for miracles?) [Quran 6:95]

The consistent laws of seeds germination allow humans to learn agricultural techniques for their benefit. If God changed the rules for seeds germination at random, people will still be living in caves. Just like there are laws for the life of new plant from an apparent dead stone like seeds, and vice versa, human life and death also follows certain rules.
Not only on earth but also in space, everything (planets, sun, and stars) follows His prescribed fixed laws. If they did not follow consistent laws, navigation and tracking would be extremely difficult.

… (He has appointed) the sun and the moon [to run their well-calculated courses [Quran 10:5]] for calculation. [So that they become a means of calculating time for you [Quran 10:5]] . Such is the Design of the All-Powerful, the Knower. [Quran 6:96]


He is the One Who has made the stars to guide you through the darkness of the land and the sea. We have scattered Our signs [throughout the Universe] for people who use their knowledge  (about never changing natural laws) . [Quran 6:97]

Just as everything in the universe follows God’s rule, so does the evolution of life.

And He is the One Who initiated you from a single life [cell]. Then  (in the process of evolution)  He appointed stages, from one station to the next destination. (Thus, goes on the journey of life.) We explain Our Messages for people who use their insight. [Quran 6:98]

section: Why God Cannot Have a Son?
text:
Why God Cannot Have a Son?
The universe is only an expression of God’s unchanging Attributes. If He has set a rule for procreation through a father and a mother, then even God cannot have a Son because He does not have a mate.
If God wanted, He could have created a Son without a Wife, but His argument is not that He cannot create a Son; His argument is that He does not have a Wife and He cannot violate the law for having a child, which requires two parents. God does not change His Sunnah.

Wonderful Originator of the heavens and earth;  how can He have a son when He never chose for Himself a mate?  He creates all things (in accordance with laws) and He is the Profound Knower of all things and events. [Quran 6:101]


What About The Virgin Birth?
How could Mary have a son without a mate if the God Himself cannot have a son without a mate? God never changes His Laws in the Universe. (Three of the four gospels mention Joseph the Carpenter as the father of Jesus.)


Did Jesus Have a Wife and Children?
His laws do not change for his messengers either. The job of a messenger is to convey the Message. The results (reckoning) will be according to God’s rules that never change for anyone.

We did send Messengers before you, and appointed wives and children for them. It was not given to any Messenger that he could bring a sign  (the requital they hastened for) , but it came according to God’s Law of Respite [also 7:34]. For every rise and fall, there is a written law [Quran 13:38]

All Messengers were mortal human beings [3:144] and they conveyed God’s Revelation as commanded. Please note that ‘all’ of them had wives and children and think of Jesus!

(O Messenger) whether We show you what We promise them, or cause you to die before that, your duty is to convey the Message. And the reckoning is Ours. [Quran 13:40]

title: The Quranic God
text:
Laws for Human Life (Psyche)
Natural laws govern the physical world, and we discover them through observation and reasoning. However, there is another set of laws that govern the non-physical world, such as the psyche, self, or “soul,” and these laws also follow a structured system. These psychological laws govern how individuals’ behaviors impact their inner selves (the Nafs) and, in turn, influence larger societal outcomes.
The laws in the non-physical world, like the natural laws, are fixed. Actions driven by lowly desires pollute and degrade the Nafs, leading to spiritual ruin, while good actions nourish and purify it, paving the way for personal and societal flourishing. The Quran highlights the importance of nourishing the Nafs:

And (regarding) the Nafs … Successful is he who nourishes/grows it. And failure is he who ruins/pollutes it. [Quran 91:7-10]

As some natural laws are more complex than others, so too are the laws in the non-physical realm. Human free will plays a pivotal role in making this system ultra-complex. Free will adds layers of unpredictability and choice, which shapes the course of individual lives and societies. However, free will does not exempt individuals from the consequences of their actions; it only allows for the freedom to choose actions.
Consider the analogy of a weather system. Countless factors contribute to the specific weather conditions at any given moment. A small change in one factor can radically alter the prediction. This unpredictability does not suggest that weather laws are non-existent, but rather that our understanding of the system is limited. Similarly, the psychological laws governing human behavior and societal outcomes are not always fully predictable due to the complexities introduced by free will.
Despite the complexity, everything in nature, except free will, follows fixed laws. Free will may allow a person to make choices, but it does not grant them control over the consequences of those choices. For example, one may choose to shoot a gun, but no matter how strong their will, they cannot undo the death caused by their action. Similarly, a leader has the freedom to speak their mind, but they cannot control the ripple effects of their words within a society. Their utterances may inspire change, for good or ill, based on the collective psyche of the people.

title: The Quranic God
text:
The Role of Free Will
The existence of free will is crucial in understanding responsibility and accountability in society. Legal systems, moral standards, and social contracts are based on the assumption that humans have the ability to choose their actions. Without free will, the concepts of right and wrong become meaningless, as individuals would not be able to choose between them.
Some neurologists argue that our actions are initiated before we consciously become aware of them, suggesting that free will does not exist. This argument primarily addresses reactionary actions that occur in high-stress or time-sensitive situations, where individuals act based on ingrained habits or instincts. While this might be true in some cases, it does not invalidate the concept of free will. Over time, habits can solidify, but we are still responsible for cultivating these reactions and for choosing whether to act upon them.
Not all actions are reactionary. In many situations, we have ample time to reflect and make decisions based on reason, rather than reflex. This capacity to deliberate and choose is what distinguishes human behavior from mere instinct or reaction. Therefore, while certain actions may be automatic, we maintain the power and responsibility to shape our actions and, by extension, our inner selves (the Nafs) over time.
Conclusion
In both the physical and psychological realms, fixed laws guide outcomes. While free will introduces complexity into the system, it does not exempt individuals from responsibility for their actions. The laws governing the Nafs emphasize the importance of nurturing good qualities while avoiding those actions that degrade the soul. Ultimately, the choices we make shape not only our inner selves but also the broader fabric of society.

title: Atheism - A Rational Approach to A-theism
text:
Science explores the observable universe, but it can’t reach beyond the Big Bang or our universe. Scientists can make hypotheses about multi-universes based on what they see here, but they have no way to prove or disprove them. Thus, science is a powerful tool for understanding our universe, but it does not have the capacity to confirm or deny the existence of God. Expecting science to prove one way or the other would tantamount to misunderstanding science.
Agnostics acknowledge this lack of scientific evidence and stay neutral on the question of God. Atheists, however, reject the existence of God, seeing no scientific reason to believe. Interestingly, logical reasoning can prove the existence of God, but only if one is open-minded.
It’s wise to distance oneself from any religion that promotes illogical dogmas, oppressive behavior, and allows atrocious acts against non-believers or followers of other faiths. However, the question of God’s existence is separate from the lies told in His name by some believers.
To find the truth, we must approach the subject rationally, examining all evidence without bias. Atheists, who pride themselves on rationality, should also rely on reason and critical thinking, avoiding speculative assumptions about a higher being.
In this discussion, we present logical arguments to prove the existence of a “Higher Being”. This term refers not to a deity bound by religious doctrine, but to an ultimate reality that exists independently and essentially, without relying on anything else. By making this distinction, we aim to foster a fair and thoughtful dialogue, free of misconceptions or prejudices.
We invite everyone to engage meaningfully with an open mind. Please, set aside societal influences and personal desires, and consider the arguments based on their merit.

title: Atheism - A Rational Approach to A-theism
text:
Existence and Reality
Before we delve into the matter, it’s worth contemplating the notion of existence. What does it mean to exist? While most people accept their existence and the world around them as self-evident, this assumption is worth examining. Consider the possibility that everything you know is part of a dream — your dream. How would you distinguish this dream from reality?
Alternatively, imagine being connected to a machine that generates a simulated reality for your mind. Your sensory experiences are manipulated, and you cannot tell that this reality is artificial. Can such a machine make you doubt your own existence? Of course not!
The very act of doubting your existence is proof that you exist, because you cannot create a doubt in someone or something that does not exist. In addition, doubt requires a conscious, self-aware entity to experience it. Therefore, while a dream or a machine might deceive your senses, it cannot erase your fundamental self-awareness.
Though experiments like these can affirm our own existence, they leave us uncertain about the nature of the reality beyond ourselves. Whether our world is real or not, the arguments we are going to present remain valid. For simplicity, we will assume that the world we observe is “real.”
Within this context, we define two types of realities: conditioned and unconditioned.

Conditioned Reality
A reality that depends on external factors for its existence at any given moment. In other words, its existence is conditional upon certain conditions being met at the moment of its existence.
For instance, you as a human being rely on organs, air, and countless other conditions to exist. All these conditions need to be present for your existence. Take, for example, a cat, which depends on its cells, molecules, atoms, etc. and their specific organization or structure to maintain its existence. These dependencies extend to everything in the observable universe, including particles, waves, and even the laws of physics.


Unconditioned Reality
A reality that exists independently, requiring no external conditions to sustain it. This is often described as an “uncaused cause” or a foundational existence.

title: Atheism - A Rational Approach to A-theism
text:
The Approach
Before proceeding to the actual arguments, it is worth recalling that proof by contradiction is a common and powerful method used in both mathematics and logic to demonstrate the validity of a statement. In the absence of observable evidence, proof by contradiction is a useful method of proving or disproving logical assertions. We intend to use this method to prove the existence of an Unconditioned Reality - the Higher Being.
Proof by contradiction works by assuming the opposite of what one wishes to prove. For example, to prove that a Higher Being exists, one assumes that a Higher Being does not exist. Then, logical arguments are presented showing that the assumption leads to a contradiction. If such a contradiction arises, it can be concluded that the assumption was wrong and not viable, thus proving the validity of the original assertion. This method works only when there are two possiblities that are disjoint - meaning one of them must be true but never both.
For an “Unconditioned Reality”, there are two mutually exclusive possibilities: either it exists or not. We will use the described method to prove its exists.

title: Atheism - A Rational Approach to A-theism
text:
The Proof
We want to prove that an Unconditioned Reality exists, and at this time, we do not know if it exists or not. But one thing is certain: you exist, and you rely on many realities for your existence. Thus, it is obvious that some realities exist.
Now, for the sake of argument, let’s assume that an Unconditioned Reality does not exist.
This assumption implies that the world consists of only conditioned realities. The set of these realities can either be finite or infinite. Let’s consider both cases one by one.


A Finite Set of Conditioned Realities (case 1)
For simplicity, consider the case of your existence. You are a conditioned reality, dependent on cells and their specific organization. The cells are conditioned realities and depend on molecules and their structures. The molecules, in turn, are also conditioned realities as they rely on subsequent realities. Let’s assume the last in the chain of these dependencies is called ‘x’.
Being a conditioned reality, ‘x’ cannot exist because the reality it depends on does not exist—recall ‘x’ is the last one in the chain. If ‘x’ does not exist, the entire chain of dependencies falls apart like a domino effect. If none of the dependent realities exist, you cannot exist either. But that is a contradiction because you exist.
Thus, the assumption of the non-existence of Unconditioned Reality leads to a contradiction; therefore, the assumption was not valid.
The same argument can also be represented by the following figure, where conditioned reality-1 depends on conditioned reality-2, which in turn depends on conditioned reality-3, and so on until the last conditioned reality-x:
reality_1← reality_2← ... reality_x←
Since the reality that reality-x depends on does not exist, none of the realities in the chain exist. The same argument can be repeated for any number of conditioned realities. In the absence of an “Unconditioned Reality,” none can exist.


Finite Set with Circular Dependency (case 2)
One could argue that the contradiction problem can be avoided if the last conditioned reality-x depends on the first conditioned reality-1. This dependency chain is shown in the following figure, where reality-1 is shown twice only for the purpose of clarity - reality-x depending on reality-1:
reality_1← reality_2← ... reality_x← reality_1←
This arrangement creates a problem of self-dependence, where reality_1 depends on itself through the chain of intermediaries. This setup implies that conditioned reality_1 must sustain, through intermediaries, its own existence, which is a logical impossibility.
A reality cannot cause its own existence because it would need to exist prior to itself to fulfill the dependency. Therefore, this arrangement also leads to a contradiction.
Both of these cases have demonstrated that a set of finite conditioned realities cannot exist, unless the assumption is invalid.


An Infinite Set of Conditioned Realities
Next, consider the case of an infinite set of conditioned realities, which can be shown in the following dependency chain figure:
reality_1← reality_2← ... reality_x← ...
Let’s first consider an alternative arrangement, for simplicity, where an infinite number of conditioned realities exist between the first conditioned reality-1 and the last conditioned reality-x, as shown below within the parenthesis:
reality_1← (... reality_y← ...) reality_x←
This arrangement is no different from the case of finite conditioned realities with reality-x being the last. As long as the reality that reality-x depends on does not exist, none of the other realities exist, even if they are infinite.
Even if you rearrange these conditioned realities where there is no last conditioned reality and the chain is infinite, the fact remains that none of those can exist on their own because all are conditioned realities. But, we know that realities exist; hence, this case also leas to a contradiction.

It is to be noted that based on how a conditioned reality was defined in terms of “simultaneous existence of dependencies,” the infinite regress challenge is not valid for this case.
Simultaneous Existence of Dependencies
For a conditioned reality to exist, all the conditions it depends on must exist simultaneously. For example, a cat cannot exist unless its cells, molecules, and atoms exist at the same time. This requirement holds for every link in the chain.
Infinite Regress
Infinite regress refers to a scenario where a chain of dependencies extends indefinitely without ever reaching a foundational cause. Imagine an infinite chain of causes and effects, where each effect depends on a prior cause. In such a scenario, the process of cause-and-effect would require infinite time to reach any particular point, making the existence of the present moment impossible.
In the current scenario, all dependent realities must exist now simultaneously for a conditioned reality to exist, even if they are infinite. This is impossible because none of them can exist on their own and rely on some other reality for their existence.

From the above cases, it becomes evident that conditioned realities cannot exist on their own, whether arranged in a finite or infinite set.
The contradictions in both scenarios demonstrate that our assumption - “no unconditioned reality exists” - is false. Therefore, the existence of an unconditioned reality is necessary to sustain all conditioned realities.
An unconditioned reality, by definition, exists independently and does not rely on any external factors. It serves as the ultimate foundation, providing the necessary support for all dependent realities.


Conclusion
We began with the assumption that no unconditioned reality exists and explored all possible configurations of conditioned realities. Each scenario led to contradictions, proving the assumption untenable. Thus, we conclude that an unconditioned reality must exist.

title: Atheism - A Rational Approach to A-theism
text:
The Uncaused, Indivisible, and One
Here, we will present the proof for the oneness of unconditioned reality.
The concept of an unconditioned reality must be “indivisible”. If it were comprised of parts or subcomponents, it would not be an unconditioned reality (consider the relationship between a cat and its components). As such, the idea of a higher being cannot be divided into two or more entities in one. By definition, this higher being must also be uncaused (not depending on any condition or cause.)
If there were “multiple” unconditioned realities, they would either be identical or differ in some aspect. If they differed, there would be some aspect of differences between them. However, this would suggest that the realities have parts (with differing and similar aspects), making them dependent on those components, which leads to absurdity (as they are unconditioned realities.) Therefore, the existence of multiple unconditioned realities is an impossibility.
The possibility of multiple “identical” realities is also eliminated. According to the principle of the Identity of Indiscernible by Leibniz, if there are multiple realities, they must be identical.
It is incorrect to consider identical realities as occupying separate areas in space, as space is part of the conditioned realities, which cannot exist independently. The idea of multiple identical unconditioned realities is therefore invalid.
Therefore, there is only One, Indivisible, Uncaused reality, commonly referred to as God or a Higher Being.

title: Objections and Questions
text:
If a proof for the existence of an Uncaused Cause exists, atheists lack a valid basis to deny the existence of God. While one might reject specific religious interpretations of how God operates in our lives or in the world, the existence of God itself cannot be reasonably dismissed. Let’s examine some of the common objections and questions raised by atheists.
The claim that “God cannot be scientifically proven” is not a sound argument but rather a reflection of the limitations inherent in our scientific methods. The absence of scientific evidence should not be mistaken for evidence against God’s existence. Science, by its nature, operates within a framework of assumptions and principles that themselves cannot be proven.
The existence of God has been demonstrated through logical and mathematical reasoning in Part 1, not mere blind faith. Recognizing the limits of scientific methods invites us to consider proofs and arguments beyond empirical evidence.
This statement misrepresents the essence of scientific understanding. Historically, even great minds like Aristotle suggested that life could arise spontaneously, a belief held by scientists for over two millennia. Similarly, contemporary statements about quantum physics are often misunderstood or oversimplified.
Quantum physics operates on the concept of the quantum field, which undergoes spontaneous fluctuations. However, the root cause of these fluctuations remains unknown. The lack of current understanding does not equate to the absence of an underlying cause. To assert otherwise is to mistake a gap in knowledge for proof of randomness or “nothingness.”
While Stephen Hawking proposed that the laws of physics could lead to the spontaneous creation of the universe, this idea requires closer scrutiny. Laws, by definition, describe how entities behave — they do not possess causal power. For instance, the law of gravity describes the attraction between masses but does not cause or generate that attraction.
This perspective also raises deeper questions: What ensures that matter consistently behaves according to these laws? What or who establishes these laws in the first place? Without addressing such fundamental issues, the claim remains incomplete and speculative.
The assertion that “the universe is eternal and infinite” is an unproven assumption. The corresponding claim that “there is no need for God” is not a scientific conclusion but a subjective perspective. Statements beginning with “if” inherently reflect hypothetical scenarios unless substantiated by evidence.
Additionally, the argument overlooks key principles, such as the second law of thermodynamics. This law illustrates that systems naturally progress towards states of higher entropy or disorder. For example, when a cup breaks, the probability of it spontaneously reassembling into its original form is nearly zero. Extending this concept, it is even more improbable for a universe of such immense complexity and harmony to arise spontaneously or exist eternally in its current state.
Despite its remarkable advancements, science remains unable to answer certain fundamental questions:
Natural laws merely describe observed behaviors; they do not explain the underlying causes of those behaviors.
By carefully reviewing the proof provided in Part 1, it becomes evident that the idea of an eternal or infinite existence of conditioned realities (like matter) is logically untenable. These conditioned realities must rely on an Uncaused Cause, usually termed as Yehweh, God, or Allah.
Contrary to this claim, proof of the One, Indivisible, Uncaused Reality has been provided in Part 1. Belief in the “non-existence” of God or the eternity of matter, however, remains a matter of blind faith. Atheists, who often emphasize rationality, offer no concrete proof for their assertions. Their arguments frequently rely on subjective reasoning or wishful thinking rather than logical and evidence-based conclusions.
The question of suffering is less a challenge to God’s existence and more an exploration of observed reality. Without a Divine Being, concepts like suffering, morality, and justice lose their objective meaning. For instance, no scientific law can label the atrocities of the Nazi concentration camps as “wrong.” Science operates in the realm of observable phenomena and measurable facts; it does not address emotions, values, or ethics.
A Divine framework is necessary to anchor these concepts. Without it, terms like “right” and “wrong” become arbitrary, defined only by human preference or societal norms.

title: Objections and Questions
text:
Clarification: Cause-and-Effect and God’s Will
The concepts of natural laws and God’s will are not mutually exclusive; rather, they coexist harmoniously. God, through His free will, upholds the natural laws that govern the universe, ensuring their consistency and reliability. While humans are endowed with free will, they remain subject to these immutable laws. For example, a person can choose to place their hand in fire, but they cannot escape the law of burning that governs the fire’s behavior.
If God were to constantly alter the behavior of elements like fire, He might be seen as inconsistent or unpredictable. A flawless creation plan does not require adjustments. Consider the analogy of computer applications: human developers must release updates to address unforeseen issues, a reflection of our limited knowledge. By contrast, God’s omniscience ensures that His plan is perfect from the start, requiring no modifications. The fixed and unchanging nature of natural laws reflects this perfection.
This consistency in natural law also underscores God’s impartiality. Natural laws apply universally, without favoritism. Fire burns both believers and non-believers alike, and gravity affects everyone equally. This universal fairness is a hallmark of God’s Kingdom, demonstrating that His justice extends to all, irrespective of their beliefs.

title: Rational Thinking
text:
Humans have the capability to think and reason. When we think rationally, we analyze past experiences, explore possibilities, evaluate evidence, and make facts-driven conclusions. But how often do we pull the entire process through? A lot of the time, we shortcut the process and call fast-thinking rational-thinking.
Consider swimming for example. You learn swimming in shallow waters before jumping into deep waters. Second, you cannot shortcut the swimming process. There are four phases in a freestyle swimming stroke: 1) catch, 2) pull, 3) exit, and 4) recovery. You swim only by completing all four phases. Third, you cannot swim half-way to the middle of the river and assume you are done for the day.

title: Rational Thinking
text:
Learning never ends
When children do not understand anything, they observe others and ask questions. Asking right questions is the first step towards understanding anything and adults teach children to formulate the questions before answering. As we grow older, we pose questions (to ourselves), find answers, and update our understanding.
For example, we update our beliefs in the light of new facts and evidence. No one now believes that magic, spirit, devil, or an angel carries the sound of a person from one part of the planet to the other when talking over a phone.

Learning does not stop at any level … It is a life-long journey.

title: Rational Thinking
section: Solving the hard questions, the wrong way
text:
Solving the hard questions, the wrong way
Some questions are hard to answer. We replace them with questions that are quicker to answer. For example, if you win or lose in a match, you may replace the question, ‘What were the reasons you won or lost?’ with ‘Is God kind or unkind to you?’ Such fast-thinking hacks, in many cases, make our reasoning unsound and our understanding of the world inconsistent.
For example, we may develop a faith-based understanding of the world that is inconsistent with reality. This happens when we are unwilling to let go of false beliefs or frivolous ideas that are dear to us. The differences between the two generate conflicting models of the future in our predictive brain. We rush to resolve the uneasiness and fear generated by ambivalence in the future (outcome).
Since we cannot change the physical laws, nor do we want to let our faith go, we box our beliefs in a separate mental chambers. We do not let any fact or evidence infiltrate these chambers that can invalidate our beliefs.


Our brain does not like inconsistent views of the world based on faith versus facts. To resolve the conflict, we compartmentalize our brain. We restrict, re-interpret, or even twist the evidence in mental chambers that guard our faith.

title: Rational Thinking
section: Thinking is neither cheap nor easy
text:
Thinking is neither cheap nor easy
Thinking is an exhaustive activity that consumes energy. The process of thinking demands your focus and time. Fact-finding activities, necessary for making an informed decision, require money and resources. As some of the resources are limited and hard to acquire, the job of rational thinking becomes riddled with hurdles.
Hurdles pave the way for a fast-thinking brain. Fast thinking brain does not waste time on deep analysis. Instead, it jumps to a conclusion in minimal time to save energy and resources. It does so based on partial data, quickly available from recent experiences, repeated memories, our likenesses and dislikes, etc.
If a decision leads to immediate gains, a strong feedback loop becomes an incentive for further fast thinking. Losses may also give you an incentive for fast thinking to save whatever you can: time, energy and resources used on rational thinking that can potentially lead to the same outcome.
Ultimately, our brain goes fully into an autopilot mode, where fast-thinking takes the driving seat of our reasoning. For example, we follow rituals because it is the most convenient thing to do that requires no thinking at all. A fast-thinking brain does not have the capacity or courage to challenge the sanity of an entire group, including our loved ones who follow the same rituals. The probability of them all going wrong is extremely low if not zero.


“How can they all be so irrational when it comes to faith while they are reasonable in other worldly affairs? In addition, if the rituals have been in practice for so many centuries, previous generations must have already vetted those beliefs, right?”


Once an action has already been taken, it is not worth looking at reasons that could make us look irrational. We ignore the facts that prove us wrong and search for information that supports our actions. Over time, the accumulated (but partial) knowledge in our favor makes our faith stronger.
Some politicians and regimes take advantage of this human weakness. They make false claims and then keep rehashing time and again. When repeated enough times, people start believing in the plausibility of the claim. Instead of asking for proof of the claim, rejectors of the false claim are asked to prove their case.

Fast thinking optimizes energy, time, and resources. Once you believe in a false claim, your brain creates a separate mental box for the claims made by the person you just believed in. You accept all those claims to be (at least somewhat) true and pass the burden of proof on to the ones who deny the claims.

In addition, humans are social animals who assign very high value to activities that generate a sense of belonging. We feel a sense of belonging to a group when we follow the unique social and religious activities that define the group. Without group identity, we feel lonely and abandoned.
Where does the fear of abandonment come from? In ancient times, a lonely and fragile human was no match for wild animals or hostile groups. Sense of belonging kept humans together and alive.
We may have killed all the wild animals and created punishment laws for hurting other humans, but the desire for belonging still lingers on strongly deep within us. Belonging to a group is not a bad idea, but we sacrifice our own identity and behave like a herd.

title: Rational Thinking
text:
Conclusion
Rationality is not about finding justification for our beliefs and actions. Rather, it is about finding truth. Desires should be kept aside, and unbiased evidence should be analyzed as objectively as humanly possible. Assumption should not be made a priori, and facts should not be ignored based on our liking or disliking. We must be ready, in all honesty, to accept the reason-based decision even if we do not like it.
The good news is that we can change at any time no matter how hard our habits might have become. Just like we have trained ourselves to act on fast thinking, we can gradually train ourselves to engage in rational thinking. The more you use your reasoning faculties, the more efficient you become at using it.

title: Inherited Religion
text:
Across the globe, humanity’s beliefs span a vast and fascinating spectrum:
For instance, if you are Muslim, non-Muslims outnumber you by a ratio of nearly 3 to 1. Similarly, Christians find themselves in a comparable minority. Yet, these numbers carry no intrinsic validation or refutation of any belief system. Truth is not determined by majority rule.
An affinity with a religion, ethnicity, or place of origin does not determine one’s capacity to distinguish right from a wrong. History is witness to the fact that individuals from all walks of life have made profound contributions to science, knowledge, and intellectual discourse. While people from all walks of life make irrational decisions quite frequently.

title: Inherited Religion
text:
Inherited Beliefs and Unquestioned Traditions
Most individuals inherit their beliefs from their families and communities, seldom pausing to critically evaluate them. Take Christians, for example: their faith is often shaped by upbringing rather than a conscious, rational choice. Children are introduced to religious practices—attending church, listening to clergy, and absorbing teachings that eventually become internalized as personal truths.
Those who dare to question these handed-down beliefs are frequently labeled heretics or non-believers, a pattern not unique to Christianity but common across religions and traditions.
This phenomenon extends beyond religion. Many cling to inherited ideologies, rarely subjecting them to scrutiny. The result is a form of intellectual stagnation, where critical thinking is sidelined by blind adherence.

title: Inherited Religion
text:
Self-Interest and Belief
When individuals deviate from inherited beliefs, it often occurs subconsciously and is influenced by personal desires. Atheists, for instance, may reject religion due to perceived irrationalities but might not fully explore alternative perspectives. The decision to abandon religion can be driven by a desire to escape certain restrictions, yet this may come at the cost of overlooking valuable insights.
Beliefs, whether religious or secular, often serve self-serving interests. Even when science debunks misconceptions, it cannot definitively disprove the existence of a higher power, leaving room for an unbiased interpretation regarding a higher being. Yet, some reject - the notion of a higher being - driven by their personal desires alone.

Herd Mentality: A Barrier to Independent Thought
Herd mentality - the tendency to adopt the beliefs and customs of one’s surroundings without critical examination - pervades human behavior. This mindset stifles individualism and discourages personal reflection.
For example, consider Michael, a devout Christian, grappling with religious dogma that contradicts his reasoning:
Michael Perspective:

“How can my parents, priests, and countless Christians, including scholars and intellectuals, all be wrong? Surely, someone among them has verified the truth of our beliefs … right?”

Diana’s Perspective: Michael’s younger sister, Diana, shares similar doubts but she resolves them differently:

“My doubts must stem from my own misunderstandings and intellectual limitations. How could my family and the multitude of Christians worldwide be mistaken?”

Michael and Diana’s Parents Perspective: Their parents echo this sentiment, relying on the sheer number of believers across generations as validation of their faith.

“How could such a vast multitude of believers, spanning across different generations and diverse backgrounds, be mistaken? It seems implausible for so many individuals to coalesce around a single belief system that is fundamentally flawed or entirely fictional!”

This pattern of thinking, whereby individuals rely on the beliefs and opinions of those around them instead of engaging in personal reflection and evaluation, epitomizes the essence of herd mentality.
Breaking free requires courage and introspection but rewards individuals with clarity, independence, and the ability to make informed choices.
Note: The choice of using Christian characters is arbitrary, which can be replaced with the choice of selecting any other religion.
The Role of Religious Scholars:
Even religious scholars, regarded as authorities, are not immune to this phenomenon. They often defer to the conclusions of past scholars, assuming their infallibility while acknowledging that current thinkers can err. Faith, they admit, sometimes requires a leap beyond intellectual reasoning — a reliance on blind faith.
The blind followers say:


… Indeed, we found our (pious) fathers upon a religion and indeed we are in their footsteps (rightly) guided! [Quran 43:22]




… they say, “Good enough for us is that upon which we found our fathers..” [Quran 5:104]


While God says:


… “(such blind followers are) deaf, dumb, and blind, so they do not use their intellect.” [Quran 2:171]

title: Inherited Religion
text:
Conclusion
Herd mentality can ensnare even the most earnest individuals, discouraging critical thinking and personal exploration of deeply held beliefs. To transcend this, we must embrace courage, question inherited traditions, and strive for personal truths. In doing so, we liberate ourselves from the constraints of collective conformity and pave the way for genuine understanding and informed decision-making.

title: Intellectual Blindness
text:
Navigating the complexities and challenges of life is no small feat, and uncovering a universal solution that addresses them is an extraordinary accomplishment. However, the greater challenge lies in communicating this solution to humanity’s vast and diverse audience. The variety of languages, cultural nuances, and levels of understanding among people make this task daunting. A one-size-fits-all approach is bound to fall short. To truly connect, one must tailor their language and communication style to resonate with each unique group. Whether speaking to an illiterate individual in a remote village or engaging with a learned scholar in academia, the delivery must align with the recipient’s level of understanding and context.
If the Quran is to serve as a timeless source of guidance for all — cutting across barriers of background, education, and culture — it must transcend the limitations of its era. Its language and style must remain as relevant and profound today as they were when first revealed. Such a text would not only address life’s intricacies and challenges but also provide enduring solutions that invite reflection and adaptation.
To achieve this, the Quran’s language must be captivating, able to hold the attention of its readers even when delving into profound psychological or philosophical concepts. Its approach would naturally blend allegories, symbols, and references to familiar elements, crafting narratives rich in meaning. These stories would not merely inform but also inspire deeper thought and contemplation.
For example, instead of presenting a dry, academic discourse on human behavior and the best courses of action, the Quran could employ vivid metaphors and imaginative analogies to make complex ideas accessible. Consider the metaphor of blindness as seen in The Country of The Blind - an evocative way to represent certain human behaviors and limitations. Such creative storytelling could serve as a powerful tool for conveying profound truths in a relatable and thought-provoking manner.

title: Intellectual Blindness
text:
Metaphors in the Quran
Metaphors in the Quran serve as powerful tools, weaving vivid illustrations that resonate deeply with readers and transcend the boundaries of time and language.
One such metaphor is ‘blindness’, symbolizing a state where individuals abandon reason and logic, allowing desires and emotions to dictate their decisions. This often leads to the unquestioning acceptance of unverified dogmas and baseless beliefs, blinding individuals to the pursuit of truth and enlightenment.
Similarly, the Quran employs ‘death’ as a metaphor to represent stagnation and decay, whether in individuals or entire societies. It depicts a condition where, despite physical existence, there is a lack of responsiveness to truth and constructive dialogue—akin to speaking to the lifeless. This metaphor underscores the need for transformative change, urging a shift towards a vibrant, purposeful, and progressive way of life.
The Quran’s masterful use of such metaphors enables it to communicate profound truths in a memorable and engaging way. By eschewing overly technical language, it appeals directly to both the intellect and the soul, making its messages accessible to people across diverse backgrounds.
This is articulated clearly in the Quran:

[Intellectually] blind and the seeing are not equal. Nor are the darknesses and the light … And the living and the dead are not alike … [Quran 35:19-22]

Here, the Quran eloquently casts itself as ‘the light’ - a luminous guide for those seeking truth and enlightenment. In contrast, everything outside its teachings is portrayed as ‘darkness’. The capacity for reasoning and intellectual inquiry is celebrated as “seeing,” while the obstinate clinging to irrational beliefs is described as “blindness.” These metaphors emphasize the essential role of reason and critical thinking in the pursuit of knowledge and understanding.
Much like navigating in pitch darkness requires light, true guidance depends on two essential elements: the Quran as the source of enlightenment (the light) and intellectual reasoning (the seeing eyes) as the means to perceive it.

Just as light holds no value without one’s ability to see, the Quran’s teachings cannot be fully grasped or applied without a discerning and reflective mind.

title: Intellectual Blindness
text:
The Blindness
The Quran repeatedly emphasizes the transformative mission of God’s messengers: to liberate humanity from the chains of false beliefs and herd mentality. These messengers sought to awaken the innate reasoning power within individuals, empowering them to discern right from wrong through the lens of logic and evidence.
Yet, despite the messengers’ tireless efforts to illuminate the path of truth, many individuals resolutely clung to their entrenched traditions and inherited beliefs. They staunchly declared, “We shall not abandon the beliefs of our forefathers, even if they defy reason. Our ancestors followed these beliefs, and so shall we.” This defiance highlights the profound grip of inherited beliefs, which often prevail even when faced with compelling evidence of their fallacy.
Consider the story of Prophet Noah, who called upon his people to abandon their fruitless idol worship. Instead of engaging in intellectual inquiry, they held steadfast to their blind faith, offering a response rooted in ancestral allegiance:

(They said,) ‘… We never heard such (a rational evaluation of faith) from our elders (and sages) of earlier generations.’ [Quran 23:23-24]

This phenomenon of intellectual blindness, often anchored in unwavering loyalty to ancestral traditions, transcends religious and cultural boundaries. Time and again, the Quran recounts similar resistance faced by various prophets, illustrating the universal nature of this challenge.
For instance, when Prophet Saleh urged his people to turn away from worshiping hollow deities, their reaction was emblematic of the stubborn adherence to inherited practices:

They said, ‘O Saleh! We had placed great hopes in you before this! But how dare you tell us to move away from worshiping what our elders worshiped? …’ [Quran 11:62]

A parallel narrative emerges with Prophet Abraham, who questioned his father and community about their devotion to lifeless statues. Their response, void of reasoning, epitomized intellectual complacency:

When he (Abraham) said to his father and his people, ‘What are these images and statues to which you are devoted (Give me some rational reasoning for your behavior)?’ They responded, ‘We found our elders worshiping them’ (Beliefs require blind following and not critical thinking.) [Quran 21:52-53]

This resistance persisted even in the face of divine revelations. Pharaoh and his followers, when confronted by Prophet Moses, dismissed his calls to reason, favoring the traditions of their ancestors:

They said, ‘Have you come to divert us (with your reasoning skills) from what we found our elders practicing? …’ [Quran 10:78]

The same pattern recurred during the time of Prophet Muhammad. Those defending their ancestral beliefs dismissed rational inquiry, accusing the Prophet of fabricating lies to deviate them from their forefathers’ traditions:

When Our Ayaat (signs) are conveyed to them in all clarity, they say, ‘This is only a man who wants to divert you from what your elders used to worship.’ and they (further) say, ‘This is nothing but an invented lie.’ … [Quran 34:43]

When invited to follow the rational guidance revealed in the Quran, they responded with unwavering loyalty to their ancestral ways:

When it is said to them, ‘Follow what (rational guidance) God has revealed (in the Quran)’, they say, ‘Nay! We will follow the ways of our elders.’ What! Even though their elders were lacking in understanding and were not rightly guided? [Quran 2:170]


Rather, they say, “Indeed, we found our elders upon a religion, and we are in their footsteps [rightly] guided.” [Quran 43:22]


… they say, ‘Enough for us is what we found our elders doing.’ What! Even though their elders had no knowledge whatsoever and no guidance?’ [Quran 5:104]


These Quranic verses vividly illustrate the persistent challenge of overcoming intellectual blindness and the unyielding grip of ancestral traditions. They serve as a timeless reminder of the importance of reason and critical thinking in the pursuit of truth and understanding.

title: Intellectual Blindness
text:
Herd Mentality
The Quran places supreme emphasis on the power of individual reasoning as the ultimate tool for discerning truth. It critiques those who blindly follow religious leaders without employing their intellect, likening them to sheep that obediently trail behind their shepherd. This behavior stems from habit and upbringing, neglecting the exercise of personal judgment and critical thinking.

The likeness of truth-rejecters (due to blind following) is that (of a sheep) which hears the shepherd’s call but hears in it nothing more than a sound and a shout (to be followed blindly). [Intellectually] Deaf, dumb, blind, for they do not use their reason [عقل]. [Quran 2:171]

In another powerful metaphor, the Quran likens those who base their beliefs solely on ancestral traditions to individuals desiring eyes in the back of their heads — perpetually looking backward instead of critically examining the reality in front of them. This metaphor underscores the futility of anchoring one’s convictions in the past while ignoring present truths.

On the Day when their faces shall be tossed about in the fire (looking backward), they will say, ‘Oh, We wish we had obeyed God, and obeyed the Messenger!’ (who asked us to ponder over what was right in front of us.) .. And they will (further) say, ‘Our Lord! We obeyed our revered clergy and the leaders and it is those who led us astray from the path .. Our Lord! Give them double punishment and banish them from Your grace.’ [Quran 33:66-68]

This stark imagery serves as a cautionary tale, urging individuals to rely on their intellectual faculties rather than succumbing to the allure of blind following or unquestioned loyalty to traditions. The Quran calls for a forward-looking perspective, rooted in reasoning and a quest for truth, to avoid the pitfalls of herd mentality.

title: Intellectual Blindness
text:
Religious Leaders and Their Followers
Religious leaders and scholars who mislead others through false teachings will face a double burden of accountability. They will not only bear the consequences of their own intellectual blindness but also the weight of leading others astray.

They shall bear their burdens undiminished on Resurrection Day, with part of the burdens of those whom they misled … Ah, evil is what they bear! [Quran 16:25]

However, followers cannot escape their own responsibility. Blindly relying on religious leaders will not absolve them of the duty to use their reasoning and judgment. These followers, too, will face the consequences of their actions. In the depths of Hell — a state described in the Quran as both inner turmoil and societal chaos devoid of peace — they will engage in bitter debates with their leaders, filled with regret for their choices.

… If you could only see these transgressors when they are made to stand before their Lord, how they blame one another. The followers will tell their proud leaders, ‘If it were not for you, we would have been believers.’ [Quran 34:31]

The Quran draws a stark comparison between those who neglect their intellectual faculties and animals, which require external restraints. Just as humans impose physical restraints on dangerous animals, God will impose shackles on those who lived without engaging their reason, behaving as if devoid of higher intellect.

… Both parties (religious leaders and their blind followers) will be filled with remorse when they see the doom. We will put shackles around the necks of all those who rejected the truth. Should they be rewarded with anything else except for what they used to do (i.e., behaving like animals)? [Quran 34:33]

This vivid depiction serves as a powerful reminder of the critical importance of intellectual accountability. It emphasizes that each individual, regardless of their role or position, must actively seek truth through reason and discernment to avoid the perils of blind following and misguided leadership.

title: Country of the Blind
text:
Long ago, a hiker lost his footing and tumbled down a mountainside, landing in a hidden valley. Centuries before, a powerful earthquake had sealed this valley off from the rest of the world with massive rocks. While outsiders believed the inhabitants had perished, the truth was quite the opposite—they survived and even flourished in their secluded haven.
Not long after the earthquake, a genetic eye disease began to spread through the isolated community. Over time, it rendered each new generation blind from birth. Facing an uncertain future, the elders of the valley dedicated themselves to crafting ingenious methods to adapt and thrive in a world devoid of sight. As centuries passed, the memory of sight itself faded into myth, and the community came to believe that blindness was the natural order of life.
When the hiker regained consciousness and surveyed his surroundings, he realized he was in what could only be described as a “Country of the Blind.” Seeing himself as the proverbial “one-eyed king,” he tried to share his knowledge of the world as perceived through sight. Yet his efforts were met with confusion. The community struggled to grasp his descriptions of birdsong’s source, the sun’s warmth, or the stars’ glittering beauty. These wonders, tied to sight, were incomprehensible to them.
To the valley’s inhabitants, the hiker was not a beacon of wisdom but an anomaly. They had honed their other senses—smell, touch, and hearing — to extraordinary levels and regarded his clumsiness as a significant flaw. His reliance on sight seemed to them a peculiar deficiency, and his attempts to describe the world clashed with their deeply rooted beliefs about their visionless reality.
Over time, their patience waned. The hiker’s constant challenges to their worldview made him an outsider in more ways than one. Declared a heretic, he was ordered to leave. But with no way out of the sealed valley, the elders allowed him to stay—on the condition that he abandon all talk of sight.
Reluctantly, the man complied. However, as he grew to love a young woman in the community, he felt compelled to reveal to her the value of sight. His efforts, however well-intentioned, alarmed the woman, who reported them to the elders. After consulting the village doctor, they reached a chilling conclusion: the man’s “sight” was a peculiar malady, causing mental anguish and irrational claims.
The doctor proposed a cure: the removal of the man’s eyes. Stripping him of sight, they reasoned, would free him from his delusions and integrate him fully into their way of life. Faced with this ultimatum, the man was forced to confront a harrowing choice—conform to their world or cling to his vision.

title: Country of the Blind
section: The Metaphors of Sight and Blindness
text:
The Metaphors of Sight and Blindness
In ‘The Country of the Blind’ by H. G. Wells, blindness serves as a metaphor for closed-mindedness, symbolizing societies resistant to new ideas and unwilling to question long-held beliefs. The valley becomes an allegory for insular communities that view inherited traditions as immutable truths, rejecting challenges and branding critical thinking as heresy.
In literature, blindness often represents intellectual stagnation, a failure to employ one’s cognitive faculties. Conversely, metaphorical “death” can signify willful indifference—ignoring efforts to awaken awareness or spark change. It embodies the dismissive refrain, “I don’t care,” and the willful rejection of growth.
This timeless narrative challenges us to examine the tension between innovation and tradition, the cost of conformity, and the courage it takes to see - and seek - a broader truth.


[Intellectually] blind and the seeing are not equal. Nor are the darknesses and the light … And [clearly] the living and the dead are not alike … [Quran 35:19-22]

title: The Quran - Reason-based Message
text:
Most people assume that Islam teaches blind faith like all other religions. But that is not the case if you read the Quran with an unbiased mind. title: The Quran - Reason-based Message

title: A Critique of Intellect
section: “Islamic Empire” and the Renaissance of Europe
text:
“Islamic Empire” and the Renaissance of Europe
The initial policies of the Islamic empire were supportive of reason-based thinking. Therefore, scientific learning and scholarship flourished throughout the empire. The conducive environment produced thousands of polymaths (scientists and scholars) during the first few hundred years.
A small list of Muslim mathematicians, astronomers, biologists, chemists, psychologists, economists, geographers, and philosophers, who were at the top of their fields in the entire world of their time, can be found on the Internet.
Al-gebra and al-gorithm are two of the most common phrases in mathematical and computer sciences, which bear the name of Muslim scientists born a thousand years ago — Geber (Jabir Bin Hayyan جابر بن حیّان ) died in 816 A.D. and Algorithmi (Al-Khwarizmi الخوارزمی ) died in 850 A.D., respectively. Whenever you see ‘al’ at the beginning of a scientific or scholarly term, chances are that it is a twisted form of an Arabic word. Hazen (Ibn al-Haytham ابن الہیثم ), Alberonius (Al-Bairuni البیرونی ) and Avicenna (Ibn-Sina ابن سینا ) were among the intellectuals whose works have survived to date, to some degree.
Although most of the original work from that era has been lost to history, it served as a steppingstone for the European Renaissance scholars and scientists. To build the scientific foundation, Europe was already translating and studying the writings of Muslim scholars by the end of the 11th century.

title: A Critique of Intellect
text:
Muhammad Iqbal’s Poetry

Al-Ghazali — The Intellect Slayer
It is said that after Al-Ghazali [1058 – 1111 A.D.] criticized the scientific approach in his landmark book, ‘Tahafat-ul-Filasafa’ [ تہافت الفلاسفة ] — ‘The Incoherence of the Scientists’, the spirit of scientific inquiry died in the Muslim lands. (Recall why scientists and scientific methods are being challenged by faith-based organizations and individuals in the U.S.A. today.)
Imam Ghazali [ امام غزالی ] begins his book with the allegations against Muslim scientists as follows:

“I have observed that there is a class of people who believe in… intelligence and insight. They have abandoned all religious rituals.. and defy the injunctions of Shariah (ritualistic laws)… for they were born into an un-Islamic atmosphere and their parents were not any better …”

Imam Ghazali continues …

“[they believe] that the mathematical, logical, physical and metaphysical sciences … are the most profound; that their excellent intelligence justifies their bold attempts to discover the Hidden Things (laws of nature via causes-and-effects); and that with … their intelligence and … accomplishments, they reject the authority of shariah laws … and believe that all such things are only sacred lies (lies in the name of sacred people) and (thus) nonsense. … They refused to be content with the religion followed by their ancestors …” (Ghazali)

If the above quoted statements ring a bell, it is not a surprise. Recall ‘The Country of The Blind’. These are the same allegations that religious scholars use against those who prefer reason to blind faith.
Imam Ghazali deals with many issues in the book, but I will go with the most fundamental topic in natural sciences that Imam Ghazali attacked: the law of cause-and-effect, which is the basis for all natural sciences.
Note: There was no separation of, or distinction between scientists and philosophers in older times. There was no separate word for a scientist; they were called philosophers. You can safely replace the word ‘philosopher’ with ‘scientist-philosopher’ when you read an older book.

The Cause-and-Effect
It was well-established among Muslim scientists that things do not depart from their natural course. If there is a cause, the effect will follow. Everything in this world follows this principle. To refute this claim, Imam Ghazali writes:

“The connection between the cause and the effect is not necessary … Take for instance any two things … burning and contact with fire; light and the rise of the Sun; death and the severance of the head from the trunk (none is due to cause and effect.) …”
“[Scientists] claim that fire is an agent of burning and whenever there is fire, it cannot stop from doing what is in its nature to do (i.e., burn) after it comes into contact with a subject.”

Imam Ghazali further explains that when you show fire to cotton, cotton turns black and disintegrates. But how can [science] claim that fire burned it? Fire does not burn the cotton; it is God who turns the cotton black and disintegrates it. God does this either by Himself or through His angels. Fire is an inanimate thing; it has no power (of its own) to burn other things. [Scientists] only see the fire coming closer to the cotton and then cotton turning black, but it is God (and not the fire) who (burns and) turns cotton black.
The argument presented here is a good argument, but I do not know how it can be twisted to deduce what has been claimed in the preface of his book? Imam Ghazali gives his own reasons.
For Imam Ghazali, there are no Hidden Secrets of nature (natural laws). It is always God Who is active in His World. He does whatever He Wills! He acts according to His Wishes. Since He wishes that cotton must burn whenever fire comes closer, He turns the cotton black.
In other words, believers in cause-and-effect start believing that fire has an inherent power to burn cotton; and thus, God is not needed. This is a violation of Islamic theology according to Imam Ghazali and all subsequent Muslim scholars.

Where Did Imam Ghazali Fail?
Imam Ghazali wanted to keep the door for miracles open, but he forgot that the Quran offers a reason-based message.

title: So What!
text:
Given that the universe operates according to fixed natural laws, one might question whether belief in God holds any real significance. However, if we accept the existence of a Creator, as previously established, it follows that what happens next is not for us to decide but rests entirely with this Creator.
If the Creator had the power to bring us into existence, it is reasonable to conclude that He could recreate us at any time. Interestingly, advancements in genetics and technology suggest that humans may one day achieve feats like transferring their minds into younger replicas derived from their genetic code. If such possibilities exist within human imagination and ingenuity, how much more plausible is it that the original Creator could gather all the necessary components — both material and immaterial — to recreate us entirely?

title: So What!
text:
Conditioned Realities [The Creation]

Or were they created out of nothing, or are they [their own] creators? Or did they create the heavens and the earths [the universe]? In fact, they are not certain [about God’s plan]. [Quran 52:35-36]


And We did not create the heaven and the earth and everything between them without any purpose, as the rejectors of truth assume. So woe, to those who have denied, from the Fire [of regret when they’ll be recreated.] [Quran 38:27]


And We did not create the heaven and the earth and everything in between for sport. Had We intended amusement, We could have found it in Our presence [and not created humans], if that had been Our Will. But We hurl the truth against the falsehood, leaving it crushed, and thus it quickly vanishes. And woe unto you for what you claim. [Quran 21:16-17]


And We did not create the heavens and the earths and what is between them for sport. We only created them [for a purpose] with Truth, but most of these [deniers] do not have knowledge. [Quran 44:38-39]

title: So What!
text:
Resurrection

And the person [mockingly] says, “Can it be that when I am dead, will I be brought out alive [again]?” Does the person not remember that We created them earlier when they were nothing [non-existent]? [Quran 19:66-67]


Did you then think that We had created you in vain [without purpose], and that you would never be returned to Us?” [Quran 23:115]


Do people not see that We created them from a [mere] sperm-drop, yet they became evident adversaries [openly challenging Me]? They argue with Us, forgetting their own creation, saying, “Who will give life to decayed bones?” Say, “He will give them life who produced them the first time; for He has knowledge of all creation.” [Quran 36:77-79]


Were We incapable of the creation the first time? Rather, they are in doubt of a new creation. And indeed We created humankind and know what their (inner) selves whisper to them, for We are closer to them than their jugular vein. [Quran 50:15-16]


And they will be presented before your Lord lining up, [and He will say], “You have certainly come to Us just as We created you the first time, although you [always] claimed that We would never appoint a time for you [to return]. And the record [of deeds] will be laid [open], and you will see the wicked in fear of what is [written] in it. They will say,”Oh, woe to us! What [kind of] record is this that does not leave anything small or big unlisted?” And they will find what they did present [before them]. And your Lord does injustice to no one.” [Quran 18:48-49]
